newsitem.title: USA: Ill. tollway debt service wont be enjoined for now.
newsitem.headline: Ill. tollway debt service wont be enjoined for now.

text.p: An Illinois judge said Thursday that while debt service will not be enjoined by a proposed preliminary injunction of Illinois State Toll Highway Authority expenditures, it could be if a permanent injunction is sought in the future.

Cook County Judge Stephen Schiller found last week that the Toll Authority practice of appropriating money without legislative oversight violated the budget requirements for state agencies under the Illinois Constitution.

Wednesday, Schiller told attorneys for the taxpayers challenging the budget practices and the Toll Authority that he would enter an order enjoining most expenditures effective Dec. 15 to give the tollway the opportunity to seek an appropriation from lawmakers.

During a hearing Thursday to prepare that preliminary injunction order, Schiller said spending on debt service may also violate state requirements, although the taxpayers challenging the practice did not seek to halt expenditures for bonds the authority has issued.
Schiller also emphasized that his order would not enjoin the collection of tolls, but only spending without the proper appropriation.
With the order in place, Toll Authority attorneys can then proceed with appeals of Schiller's ruling. They have said they will ask the Illinois Supreme Court to review the case directly.
